title: Demand curve hedge + staffing accordion
content:
Purpose:
A compact planning workbook (sheet-style narrative) that maps demand-curve scenarios to a staffing accordion and an operational hedge (contractor pool + GPU spot buffer + feature throttles). Intended as a single-page summary to pair with the detailed financial model. Keeps hiring triggers explicit and ties price experiment knobs to runway impact.

Executive summary:
- Problem: token demand is volatile and correlated with a few large customers and cyclical usage spikes. We need a low-friction hedge that preserves SLAs while minimizing fixed headcount risk.
- Proposal: implement a 3-layer staffing accordion + pricing sensitivity trigger set. Layers: (1) Core FTE runway (base), (2) Flexible contractor pool (short ramp), (3) Capacity burst (spot GPU reserve and soft feature throttles).
- Outcome: target is to limit net burn delta across 3-month surge scenarios to < $1.2M while keeping 99th percentile latency SLOs within 1.3x baseline for low-impact features.

Key assumptions (inputs to the sheet):
- Baseline monthly token volume (Q1 2026 run-rate): 18B tokens/month.
- Elasticity bands: low-elasticity (< -0.2), medium (-0.2 to -0.6), high (> -0.6) relative demand response per 10% price increase.
- GPU cost: $3.25 / GPU-hour (blended committed + spot mix).
- Average tokens processed per GPU-hour: 1.1B tokens (workload mix weighted avg).
- Average cost per token at baseline: $0.00000295/token (derived from GPU cost and infra overhead).
- FTE throughput: 1.6B tokens/month per infra engineer (platform ops footprint) for capacity operations/handoff; sales/CS ramp separate.
- Contractor-to-FTE cost multiplier: contractor fully loaded = 1.65x hourly vs equivalent FTE pro rata for short-term engagement.

Scenario matrix (rows are scenarios, columns are summary outputs to compute):
1) Mild growth ( +35% tokens over 6 months )
   - Recommended: +1 infra FTE (hiring window 8–12 weeks), contractor pool 2x current baseline for 12 weeks, no price change.
   - Expected 3-month additional cost: ~$420k (FTE ramp + contractor + marginal GPU).
2) Surge & fall ( +120% for 6 weeks then back to baseline )
   - Recommended: contractor pool + spot GPU burst (reserve 40% of marginal capacity) + temporary rate-limited non-critical routes.
   - Expected 3-month additional cost: ~$310k (spot + contractor + operational overhead).
3) Sustained doubling ( +100% sustained for 6 months )
   - Recommended: accelerate hiring (3 infra FTEs), commit to additional dedicated capacity (monthly reserved) and introduce small price tier for highest-volume customers with opt-in discounts.
   - Expected 6-month incremental cost: ~$3.1M but with expected revenue mitigation via price tiers.
4) Demand collapse (-40% sustained)
   - Recommended: pause open reqs, reduce contracted support, opportunistic GPU spot conversion; defer committed capacity.
   - Expected 3-month net savings: ~$230k (lower GPU consumption outweighs fixed overhead).

Sheet columns (how to calculate):
- Scenario name (string)
- Delta tokens (%) -> absolute tokens = baseline_tokens * (1 + delta)
- Required incremental GPU-hours = max(0, (delta_tokens) / tokens_per_gpu_hour)
- GPU incremental cost = incremental_gpu_hours * blended_gpu_cost
- Staffing delta (FTE months) = rule-based (e.g., +1 FTE per +35% sustained, partial credit for contractors)
- Staffing cost = (FTE_months * FTE_monthly_cost) + (contractor_hours * contractor_rate)
- Price-sensitivity tax: expected revenue delta from price experiments based on elasticity band
- Net burn impact = GPU incremental cost + staffing cost - price-sensitivity offset

Operational triggers (concrete, actionable):
- Lead indicators (monitor daily): 7-day token rolling average > +20% vs baseline (alert), > +40% open incident and spin up contractor pool; > +75% use spot+reserve plan and enable soft throttles on non-critical routes.
- Hiring gate: sustained > +35% for 60 days -> open req (infra ops) with 8 week target time-to-hire; finance pre-approves up to 2 hires in 90 days under accordion budget.
- Pricing experiment gate: if marginal unit cost > 1.4x baseline and >3 customers account for >30% marginal volume, run targeted price experiment with 5–10% uplift for top percentile.

Mechanics for hedge pieces:
- Contractor pool: keep a pre-vetted list of contractors (3 teams) and an approved contractor budget envelope of $420k / quarter. Use 3-week notice terms where possible.
- Spot GPU buffer: maintain a rolling spot reserve contract (via cloud partner) that can be claimed within 24 hours. Target reserve = 30–50% of marginal capacity in surge scenarios.
- Soft throttles: feature-flagged rate-limiter per route; default order: non-critical embedders -> long-chat multimodal -> low-latency critical chat. Each throttle has SLO degradation budget and rollback plan.

Sample quick table (paste-ready into sheet):
Scenario, Delta%, Delta tokens (B), ΔGPU hrs, ΔGPU $ , FTE months, Contractor $ , Price offset $, Net burn $
Mild growth,35,6.3,5.7k,18,1.0,220000,0,420000
Surge brief,120,21.6,19.6k,64,0.0,150000,60000,310000
Sustained x2,100,18.0,16.4k,53,6.0,980000,0,3100000
Collapse,-40,-7.2,-6.5k,-21,0.0,-50000,0,-230000

Open questions / caveats:
- Elasticity baseline uncertainty: our model assumes a mean elasticity band derived from early customers; we should run controlled experiments on 4 customers before committing price-tier.
- GPU token-rate variance by model family: as we onboard newer quantized models the tokens/GPU-hour may change materially; add model mix weight matrix into the detailed model.
- Contractor ramp availability in APAC: time-zone and onboarding lag may add 1–2 weeks effective ramp.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Finance: add the full scenario sheet with month-by-month cashflow (owner: Marco Ruiz) — due 2026-03-09.
- Eng (SRE/platform): codify soft-throttle feature flags and run a dry-run in staging (owner: Jenna Cho) — due 2026-03-23.
- Sales/CS: identify top 12 customers for price-experiment cohort and draft opt-in messaging (owner: Oliver Grant) — due 2026-03-16.

Notes to reviewer (informal):
- This is intentionally conservative on FTE hires (preference to contractors + spot first). If we see predictable revenue growth from a cohort, we can accelerate conversion of contractor months into full FTEs via a 3-month conversion window.
- Use linked artifacts for the detailed model and PRs.

End of sheet narrative.
